# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 11 (SOPHIA Consensus)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 11
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Consensus Translation

1. But let us also inquire whether the Lord was careful to prefigure both the water and the cross. Concerning the water, it is written in reference to Israel that they would not receive the baptism that brings the forgiveness of sins, but would construct one for themselves.
2. For the prophet says: "Be astonished, O heaven, and let the earth shudder greatly at this, for this people has done two evil things: they have forsaken me, the spring of living water, and they have hewn out for themselves a cistern of death."
3. "Is my holy mountain Sinai a desolate rock? For you shall be as the nestlings of a bird when the nest is taken away."
4. And again the prophet says: "I will go before you and level mountains and break the gates of bronze and crush the bars of iron; and I will give you hidden, dark, invisible treasures, that you may know that I am the Lord God."
5. And: "You shall dwell in a lofty cave of a strong rock." And again: "His water is faithful; you shall see the King in his glory, and your soul shall meditate upon the fear of the Lord."
6. And again in another prophet he says: "The one who does these things shall be as the tree planted by streams of water, which will yield its fruit in due season, and its leaf will not wither; and whatever he does will prosper.
7. Not so the ungodly — they are like chaff which the wind blows away from the face of the earth. Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the council of the righteous."
8. Do you see how he described the water and the cross together in one type? For he says: "Blessed are those who set their hope on the cross and go down into the water." When he speaks of the reward "in its season" — at that time I will render to you; when he says "its leaf shall not wither" — he means that every word coming from your mouth in faith and love shall be for the conversion and hope of many.
9. And again another prophet says: "And the land of Jacob was glorified above all the earth." He means: he glorifies the vessel of his Spirit.
10. What then does he say? "And there was a river flowing on the right hand, and from it beautiful trees sprang up; and whoever eats of them shall live forever."
11. This means: we go down into the water bearing our sins and uncleanness, and we come up bearing our fruit in the heart, having fear and hope in Jesus in our spirit.

---

## Council Notes

- v.2: Jeremiah 2:12-13 (LXX) — "two evils" of Israel: forsaking God (the spring of living water) and constructing their own cistern. Barnabas applies this to the rejection of Christian baptism.
- v.8: "Blessed are those who set their hope on the cross and go down into the water" — this is not a known canonical or OT text; it may be a liturgical formula used at baptisms, or Barnabas's own composite construction. It is significant as one of the earliest explicit connections of the cross and baptism.
- vv.6-7: Psalm 1:3-5 (LXX). The tree by the water = the baptized Christian. This is the most explicit christological-baptismal reading of Psalm 1 in early Christian literature.
- v.10: Ezekiel 47:12 / Revelation 22:2 — the river and life-giving trees. Barnabas appears to draw on an Ezekiel tradition also used in Revelation; the water flowing from the sanctuary = baptism.
- v.11: This is the clearest theological statement of baptismal theology in the epistle: entry (sin/uncleanness) → transformation → emergence (fruit/fear/hope). The pattern is exactly the baptismal theology of Romans 6:3-4.
